idea-plugin.name: Test Quest
idea-plugin.description: Gamified learning for Selenium test automation. Generates actionable locator, coverage, and behavioral quests from test code and DOM snapshots, then verifies them deterministically before awarding points.
idea-plugin.change-notes: Version 0.1.11 isolates the snapshot agent's Byte Buddy classes from other versions on the Selenium test classpath, so Java 17 classes can be read even when the test project depends on an older Byte Buddy. Version 0.1.10 captures Selenium commands through RemoteWebDriver without transforming RemoteWebElement, which failed on some Java 17 test classpaths. Driver hook failures now include their stack trace. Version 0.1.9 also observes Selenium driver commands for snapshot capture and reports hook installation, page source failures, and the first saved HTML path in the JUnit console. Version 0.1.8 fixes a binary incompatibility that prevented the Test Quest tool window from showing its content in version 0.1.7. Version 0.1.7 displays XP progress in a theme-aware label below the bar so the text remains readable before the bar fills. Version 0.1.6 refreshes the bundled snapshot agent when it changes. The JUnit test console now confirms agent startup and reports the first snapshot capture failure, making missing snapshots diagnosable. Version 0.1.5 stores each Gemini request, raw response, and generated tasks JSON under .testquest/llm/ in the opened test project. Coverage validation accepts a new test method with different whitespace, annotations, or a throws clause while still running the named test. Fixed document saving from the Get 3 quests and Verify selected buttons on IntelliJ IDEA build 262 by scheduling it in a write-safe application context before starting background work. Added support metadata for IntelliJ IDEA builds 262.* (including IU-262.10968.63), retaining support for builds 243 through 261. Quest verification now targets the exact requested JUnit test method. Coverage quests run the newly added method, while locator and behavioral quests run the named existing method. Older saved quests remain compatible and fall back to class-level verification.
